portability_contract.shared_logic: Separate application/document algorithms from platform adapters.
portability_contract.display: Query dimensions and attributes; use semantic colors and clipping.
portability_contract.memory: Bounded buffers and handles for banked objects; report allocation failures.
portability_contract.storage: Versioned, explicitly encoded records; no persisted pointers or raw C structures.
portability_contract.migration: Recompile for the target, adapt OS-specific modules and test resource limits. This does not expand the listed supported platforms.

implementation_design.status: Accepted design baseline; implementation conformance and measured performance remain to be validated.
implementation_design.title: BPI transactional client/server v1
implementation_design.architecture: Thin Z80/ERA clients send bounded business operations to an Artemis PRO server. Query evaluation, indexes, validation, accounting posting and transactions execute on the server; clients do not fetch arbitrary database pages.

transactions.concurrency: Single serialized writer for v1 with short transactions and bounded reader locks; no long interactive transaction while a user edits a form.
transactions.commit: Append checked log records and a commit marker, force them to durable storage, then acknowledge. Apply/replay committed changes idempotently.
transactions.recovery: On startup validate checksums and recover committed log records; incomplete transactions never become visible. Use shadow page/index replacement or another explicitly validated torn-write-safe method.
transactions.failure: Do not claim durable commit until disk/controller completion semantics are proven; no battery-backed cache is assumed.
transactions.log_format: Redo-only changed-record/page after-images with transaction ID, sequence, length and checksum; the commit marker covers transaction record count and checksum. Persist duplicate-suppression outcomes in the same transaction.
transactions.buffer_policy: Do not write uncommitted changes to database files (no-steal); cap transaction size to available transaction buffers.
transactions.checkpoint: Write replacement pages and indexes to new locations, force them, then alternate checksummed generation-numbered root/checkpoint records. Retain the preceding valid root and necessary redo log until the new checkpoint is durable.

protocol.transport: Length-framed requests over TCP; bounded messages and chunked results.
protocol.duplicate_suppression: Store committed write request IDs and outcomes durably. After reconnect, clients query status or retry with the same ID; never post the same payment twice.

data_integrity: Amounts use explicitly scaled integers/decimal rules, never unspecified binary floating-point rounding.
Record currency, rounding, posting dates, account periods and unique document IDs.
Cross-module posting is atomic and produces an append-only audit record.
operations: Role-based authorization and server-side input validation
Backup captures a consistent checkpoint plus required logs; test restoration onto a clean disk.
Bounded log growth, disk-full handling and operator-visible recovery status
Plan backups and report traffic around the negotiated shared 100/250/500/1000 kbit/s raw LAN budget and measured payload throughput; slower admitted hosts limit the whole network.

initial_limits.client_policy: Bounded pages of results and forms; no entire-table download or whole-document duplication.
